Hi Samantha — great to chat this morning. Quick recap + concrete next steps so we can align on pricing and procurement timelines.

Summary of usage and budget you shared:
- Peak traffic: ~12k requests/hour initially; expected ramp to 50k reqs/hour over 6 months.
- Average tokens per request: ~480 (prompt + expected 1–2 turns of context).
- Target procurement cadence: Q2 start, 12-month term if economics align.
- Ballpark procurement budget: $40k–$120k/month (you said legal/proc will confirm a committed range).

Key ask we have for modeling: please confirm monthly token volume range. For now we modeled three ramps: conservative (50M tokens/mo), mid (200M tokens/mo), high (750M tokens/mo).

Caching assumptions we discussed (prefix cache + session KV):
- Prefix cache hit rate (first-pass query templates): baseline 35% (range 25–50% depending on prompt standardization).
- Session KV warm hits for multi-turn flows: additional 10–18% effective token reduction on average.
- Effective combined hit adjustment applied to generation tokens only (we assume prompt tokens still billed).

Attached: prefix_cache_assumptions_v1.xlsx with the modeling workbook and a draft SOW (BrightPath_SOW_draft_v1.docx).

Next steps:
1) Can you confirm the monthly token volume you want us to model (pick low/mid/high above) by EOD Monday?
2) If procurement wants an example invoice, we can provide a 1-page cost table showing effective $/1M tokens at 20/35/50% cache hit rates.
3) Propose a follow-up call week of Jan 25 to align on contractual terms and security checklist.

Thanks — I’ll loop Marcus & Karthik on modeling questions.

Best,
Irene

Samantha — per your ask, attached is the one-page table and short notes. Quick highlights below (numbers illustrative):

Scenario assumptions (baseline list price):
- List: $1,000 / 1M generation tokens; $200 / 1M prompt tokens.
- Prompt share: 35% of tokens; generation share: 65%.

Effective $/1M by combined cache hit (generation-side only):
- 20% total hit -> effective $/1M = $820
- 35% total hit -> effective $/1M = $650
- 50% total hit -> effective $/1M = $490

Monthly spend examples for mid-volume (200M tokens/month total):
- No cache: $1,000 * 0.65 * 200 = $130,000 (generation) + $200 * 0.35 * 200 = $14,000 (prompt) => $144,000
- 35% hit: generation billed = 0.65 * (1 - 0.35) * 200 = 84.5M -> $84,500 + prompt $14,000 => $98,500
- 50% hit: generation billed = 65M * (1 - 0.50) * 200/200? (note: see attached for exact calc) -> effective monthly ~$74,000

Notes on implementation impact:
- Higher prefix hit requires standardizing top-10 templates and routing those requests through a cached path. That is a product change on your side but relatively low lift (template registry + a lightweight classifier).
- Session KV warm requires sticky sessions (cookie or token) and small per-session KV storage; adds modest memory overhead but improves multi-turn LLM costs.

Next steps:
1) Is the mid-volume (200M/mo) the right scenario for the procurement one-pager? If not, tell us which bucket.
2) If procurement signs off on a 12-month commit, we can propose a tiered discount schedule tied to committed tokens/month.
3) Propose a contract review call Jan 27 — send 45-min slot options and we’ll bring legal and engineering.

If helpful I can also produce a short technical note (1 page) on the prefix classifier and session KV requirements for your product team.

Thanks — looking forward to the confirmation so procurement can move.

Best,
Irene
